clue.text: Bed for mum? That's lucky

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a thing that brings luck

blocks.note: MA is mum; read as a possessive, the bed belonging to mum is MA'S
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to have found a bed for their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: A bed for mum is mum's cot, written MA'S COT; the clue's order puts the bed first but the possessive puts mum first.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept because it is believed to bring good luck.

clue.text: Born: a new rule for old PM

indicators.note: something new has been made over, so the preceding letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A fresh rule is introduced by a long-dead prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Bonar Law was British Prime Minister in 1922-23.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonar Law led the Conservative government briefly in the 1920s, so he is a former British premier.

clue.text: A kind of welcome cardiograph?

definitions.note: the answer here works as an adjective in 'a ticker-tape welcome'
a whimsical noun: tape recording the ticker

blocks.note: first meaning: the paper streamers thrown at a parade for heroes
second meaning, playful: ticker is slang for the heart, and a cardiograph prints its beat on tape

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as a joke: a heart trace is literally tape for the ticker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker tape was the paper strip from stock telegraphs, thrown as confetti at celebratory parades in New York.

clue.text: Range in figures under a pound

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it, so the figures follow

blocks.note: taken as written
a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen
nines are figures, numerals

explanation.surface: Prices for something come in at below a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places one piece below another; pound is the animal enclosure, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain chain running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Drifter ending in rags at this time

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last of rags is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of rags
now means at this time

explanation.surface: A tramp ends up dressed in rags at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drifter' suggests a vagrant, which fits the rags; it is really the stuff that piles into drifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is blown by the wind into drifts, so it is a playful name for something that drifts.

clue.text: Climbing up, wayfarer grabs small fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards
to grab is to take hold of, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: a nomad is a wanderer
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A walker climbing a hill picks a small piece of fruit along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small purple plum.

clue.text: Minister split trousers always

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser something is to pocket it, so one word takes the other inside

blocks.note: to rend is to split or tear
ever means always

explanation.surface: A clergyman has ripped his trousers yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split trousers' reads as torn clothing; 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets, with 'split' supplying the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title of a Christian minister, used as a noun for a clergyman.

clue.text: Devoted, a group getting behind party

indicators.note: getting behind something means following it, so the group is placed after the party

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
a ring is a group, such as a gang of smugglers

explanation.surface: A committed band of supporters falls in behind a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting behind' sounds like support, but it places the group after the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adoring is full of loving devotion, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Good, soft light

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
low, as of a voice, means soft

explanation.surface: A gentle light is pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of a lamp, but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A glow is a steady, gentle light such as embers give off.

clue.text: Vessel returning in long boat

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word reads right to left
in places one word inside another

blocks.note: a can is a container, a vessel
to long for something is to pine

explanation.surface: A ship comes home inside a longboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'long boat' both look nautical; the vessel is a can and long is the verb to pine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat, historically a ship's tender.

clue.text: Series of severe measures hit NI county

blocks.note: to crack is to hit sharply
County Down is in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A tough set of security measures strikes a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a firm official campaign of strict enforcement against something.

clue.text: Junk in window, a steal

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the end of window, then a, then the start of steal

explanation.surface: Rubbish displayed in a shop window is being sold at a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is rubbish or unwanted material, the same as junk.

clue.text: Roof worker fired up again after being laid back

indicators.note: laying something back turns it the other way, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: relit means set alight once more

explanation.surface: A roofer is fired up again after being laid off for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired up' suggests enthusiasm or dismissal; here it is literal rekindling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles, and roofs are a main place tiles are fixed.

clue.text: Encircled by him, men seized monster

definitions.note: used here as an adjective, as in a monster sale

indicators.note: being encircled means lying inside, so the letters are found within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run from inside him across men into seized

explanation.surface: A man and his companions capture a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monster' reads as a noun for the captured beast, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: As an informal adjective monster means enormous, a synonym of immense.

clue.text: Underground worker inspiring awe, extraordinary communicator

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word takes the other inside

blocks.note: a miner works underground
dread is fearful awe

explanation.surface: A miner who commands respect turns out to be a remarkable speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring awe' reads as a phrase praising the miner; inspiring means breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind-reader supposedly picks up thoughts directly, a communicator with unusual telepathic powers.

clue.text: Travel bug, result of flea-bites on walkers?

blocks.note: first meaning: the restless urge to travel
second meaning, literal: walkers are what we walk on, and bites make them irritate

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a literal reading of an idiom; bug and flea both play on insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet is an idiom for a restless desire to move on or travel.

clue.text: Novel man put together for team

blocks.note: novel means new
a castle is a chess piece, and chessmen are called men
united means joined, put together

explanation.surface: A fictional character is assembled to fit into a squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel man' looks like a character in a book; man is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle United is an English Premier League football club, a sports team.

clue.text: Regardless of what's in a vacuum?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase: no matter is present in empty space

blocks.note: first meaning: whatever happens, irrespective
second meaning, literal: a vacuum contains nothing physical at all

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the physics joke: a true vacuum holds no substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning irrespective of circumstances, as in no matter what.

clue.text: Solid bangle: it proving malleable

indicators.note: malleable metal can be bent into a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sturdy bracelet turns out to be soft enough to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' and 'malleable' make a deliberate contradiction about a metal bangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible means able to be touched, real and concrete, which is what solid means here.

clue.text: Award bagged by American subject for play

indicators.note: something bagged is put inside a sack, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: math is the American name for mathematics, a school subject
Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: An American wins a prize for a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American subject' reads as a citizen of the USA; it is a school subject spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's tragedy of the ambitious Scottish thane.

clue.text: Cold peak in Cumbria, mountainous

indicators.note: in a down clue the peak of a word is its top, its opening letter

blocks.note: the top letter of Cumbria
hilly land is mountainous

explanation.surface: A cold mountain summit in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold peak' wants to be a phrase for a summit; peak points to the top letter. Cumbria is the county of England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means unpleasantly cold, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Approach race ahead

blocks.note: to race is to run
up means ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: Someone is told to come nearer and dash in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach to a jump or a bowling delivery, or the period leading to an event.

clue.text: Horror film taken in by tipsy choirboys

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: the letters span the end of tipsy and the start of choirboys

explanation.surface: Drunken choristers get fooled by a scary movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 horror thriller.

clue.text: Coloured membrane in flower

blocks.note: first meaning: the coloured ring of the eye
second meaning: a plant with sword-shaped leaves

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a petal's tissue; the two halves are separate senses joined by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the pigmented part of the eye around the pupil, and also a garden plant.

clue.text: Initially town house inexpensive, essentially for a nicker?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A cheap town house is mostly suitable for someone who pinches things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' looks like an indicator for middle letters, but it is just another word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, so a nicker is someone who steals.

clue.text: Get rid of blazer?

blocks.note: first meaning: dismiss from a job
second meaning: something that blazes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' reads as a jacket you might discard; the question mark signals it means a thing that blazes.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to sack them, and a fire is a burning blaze.

clue.text: Ceremony in country during days of biblical fasting

indicators.note: during means within a span, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: Jesus fasted forty days in the wilderness
Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: A national ritual is held during a religious fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A formality is a set procedure or ritual observance, close in sense to a ceremony.

clue.text: Green: two-thirds of all bananas develop

indicators.note: keeping two parts in three of a three-letter word means one letter is dropped
bananas means crazy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the word all with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Unripe bananas will mostly ripen in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' and 'bananas' suggest unripe fruit; bananas is the slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop a photograph to a bigger size is to enlarge it; more generally both mean expand.

clue.text: Deceitful conduct in the last broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Underhand behaviour appeared in the final programme to air.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, secretive action, originally meaning theft, so it fits deceitful conduct.
